sentences.en: Throughout this election, one state has been at the center of every imaginable path to victory.
sentences.zh: 在这场选举中，有一个州始终处于通往胜利的所有可能路径的核心。

sentences.en: Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Hello, Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 你好，宾夕法尼亚。

sentences.en: We love Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我们爱宾夕法尼亚。

sentences.en: Both candidates have campaigned there relentlessly.
sentences.zh: 两位候选人都在那里进行了不懈的拉票。

sentences.en: This fall, Pennsylvania is living up to its nickname as the Keystone State.
sentences.zh: 今年秋天，宾夕法尼亚州正不负其“基石州”的称号。

sentences.en: Pro-Harris groups are spending roughly 10 times as much as pro-Trump groups in key battleground states.
sentences.zh: 在关键摇摆州，支持哈里斯的团体花费大约是支持特朗普的团体的10倍。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 我的天哪。

sentences.en: And both parties spent more money there than in any other state.
sentences.zh: 而且两党在那里的花销都超过了其他任何一个州。

sentences.en: CBS News polling shows both former President Donald Trump and Vice President Kamala Harris a neck and neck in the Keystone State.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻频道的民调显示，前总统唐纳德·特朗普与副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯在这个基石州不相上下。

sentences.en: What's very clear is that Pennsylvania is like just absolutely crucial, pivotal for them.
sentences.zh: 很明显的一点是，宾夕法尼亚对他们来说绝对是至关重要、生死攸关的。

sentences.en: And now, it's a dead heat.
sentences.zh: 而现在，双方难分伯仲。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Campbell Robertson on a consequential shift that is reshaping the map in Pennsylvania, making it the key not just to this election, but to elections to come.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事坎贝尔·罗伯逊将探讨一场正在重塑宾夕法尼亚州政治版图的重大转变，这使其不仅成为本次选举的关键，也成为未来选举的关键。

sentences.en: It's Friday, October 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月25日，星期五。

sentences.en: So, Campbell, you cover Pennsylvania for The Times.
sentences.zh: 那么，坎贝尔，你负责《时报》的宾夕法尼亚州报道。

sentences.en: Explain why Pennsylvania is being talked about as the most important state in this election.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲为什么宾夕法尼亚州被视为这次选举中最关键的州。

sentences.en: So, that is largely because Pennsylvania carries a treasure trove of 19 electoral votes.
sentences.zh: 这主要是因为宾夕法尼亚州拥有19张宝贵的选举人票。

sentences.en: It's the most electoral votes of any of the swing states.
sentences.zh: 它是所有摇摆州中选举人票最多的。

sentences.en: Now, Pennsylvania has always been close in presidential years.
sentences.zh: 在总统大选年，宾夕法尼亚的选情一直都很胶着。

sentences.en: But for a long time, it was pretty reliably democratic.
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，它相当稳定地倾向于民主党。

sentences.en: And this is largely because in places like western Pennsylvania, where you have all these union voters
sentences.zh: 这主要是因为在宾夕法尼亚州西部这样的地方，有大批工会选民

sentences.en: who have this loyalty to the party that lasted even after the steel mills closed and the factories closed, they remain loyal democratic voters.
sentences.zh: 他们对党派有着忠诚度，这种忠诚甚至在钢厂和工厂关闭后依然存在，他们一直是忠实的民主党选民。

sentences.en: But then 2016 came.
sentences.zh: 但随后2016年来了。

sentences.en: And when Donald Trump started making his speeches about American decline, about pessimism, a lot of these folks who were in places where mills and factories had closed,
sentences.zh: 当唐纳德·特朗普开始发表关于美国衰落、关于悲观情绪的演讲时，许多身处钢厂和工厂关闭之地的民众，

sentences.en: heard that and thought, that man is saying things I have been wanting to hear for a long time from a politician.
sentences.zh: 听到这些便想：这个人说出了我长久以来一直想从政客那里听到的话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, they turned out for him in big numbers.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们大批大批地出来投票支持他。

sentences.en: And 2016, Pennsylvania went for Trump, as did the election.
sentences.zh: 在2016年，宾夕法尼亚支持了特朗普，大选结果也是如此。

sentences.en: And that was the first time it had gone for a Republican presidential candidate since before 92.
sentences.zh: 这也是自1992年之前以来，该州首次支持共和党总统候选人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, huge sea change in the politics of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 所以，宾夕法尼亚的政治发生了巨大的沧海桑田般的巨变。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it illustrated what may be even a bigger sea change in American Party politics.
sentences.zh: 这说明了美国党派政治中可能更深刻的巨变。

sentences.en: You had this growing gap between voters who did not have college degrees, many of whom had great long-time careers in these steel mills and factories,
sentences.zh: 当时出现了这样一道不断扩大的鸿沟：一边是没有大学学历的选民，其中许多人在这些钢厂和工厂里拥有长期且美好的职业生涯，

sentences.en: and they were increasingly voting for the Trump Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 他们越来越多地投票给特朗普的共和党。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, you had these suburban Republicans, professionals, lawyers, and doctors, and that kind of thing,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，另一边是郊区的共和党人、专业人士、律师和医生之类的人，

sentences.en: who were starting to leave the Republican Party, or if not leave the party, vote for the Democratic candidate.
sentences.zh: 他们开始离开共和党，或者即使没有退党，也会投票给民主党候选人。

sentences.en: And so, education level became one of the most reliable indicators of how a person is going to vote at the national level.
sentences.zh: 因此，教育水平成为了预测一个人在国家层面将如何投票的最可靠指标之一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it is hard to overstate just how substantial that change has been.
sentences.zh: 而且这种变化有多大，怎么强调都不为过。

sentences.en: I used to do, as you know, demographics reporting, and, you know, it's remarkable just how much it's changed.
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，我过去做过人口统计报道，你知道，它改变的程度之大令人惊叹。

sentences.en: Education was no predictor at all.
sentences.zh: 教育曾经根本不是一个预测指标。

sentences.en: And now, it kind of tells you the answer in some way of how people are going to vote.
sentences.zh: 而现在，它在某种程度上告诉你人们会如何投票的答案。

sentences.en: That was 2016.
But 2020, we saw kind of something different, right?
sentences.zh: 但在2020年，我们看到了有点不一样的情况，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, Biden won Pennsylvania in 2020.
sentences.zh: 嗯，拜登在2020年赢了宾夕法尼亚。

sentences.en: Barely.
sentences.zh: 险胜。

sentences.en: But he won Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 但他确实赢了宾夕法尼亚。

sentences.en: And part of that is due to his strength among some of those non-college working-class voters who like that Scranton Joe pro-union guy reputation.
sentences.zh: 部分原因归功于他在那些非大学毕业的工薪阶层选民中的优势，他们喜欢那种“斯克兰顿·乔”式的亲工会形象。

sentences.en: But what really helped Biden win the state was the suburban professionals coming out in huge numbers for Biden.
sentences.zh: 但真正帮助拜登赢得该州的，是郊区专业人士大批涌出来支持拜登。

sentences.en: So, while it is true that Biden stemmed the bleeding a little bit on the education divide, he also benefited from it in these suburban voters when he won Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管拜登在一定程度上遏制了教育鸿沟带来的失血，但在他赢得宾夕法尼亚时，他也确实从这些郊区选民身上获益了。

sentences.en: So, what are the dynamics in this election?
sentences.zh: 那么，这次选举中的动态是怎样的？

sentences.en: And maybe start with Harris.
sentences.zh: 也许可以从哈里斯开始说起。

sentences.en: So, the Harris campaign strategy is pretty straightforward.
sentences.zh: 所以，哈里斯的竞选策略非常直接。

sentences.en: Drive-up turnout in the cities, particularly drive-up turnout in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 提高城市地区的投票率，特别是大幅提高郊区地区的投票率。

sentences.en: And these are where all those college-educated voters, Democrats, and even non-Trump Republicans live.
sentences.zh: 所有那些受过大学教育的选民、民主党人，甚至非特朗普的共和党人都住在这些地方。

sentences.en: And try to get those margins really high.
sentences.zh: 并试图将这些优势差距拉得非常大。

sentences.en: And then in the rural areas, and a lot of these are these non-college working-class voters, try to lose by less.
sentences.zh: 然后在农村地区，其中许多人是非大学学历的工薪阶层选民，尽量少输一些。

sentences.en: Try to keep those losing margins to a level that they can be offset by the numbers they get in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 尽量把失利的差距控制在一个能够被他们在郊区获得的票数所抵消的水平。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, we have the education dynamic coming in as a pretty essential part of her campaign.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到，教育动态成为了她竞选中至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: So, given that, Cam, what does the landscape look like for Trump in Pennsylvania?
sentences.zh: 鉴于此，坎贝尔，特朗普在宾夕法尼亚州的选情格局是怎样的？

sentences.en: So, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, Trump is really going all-in on working-class Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，特朗普真的在宾夕法尼亚州的工薪阶层身上全押上了。

sentences.en: He's visiting a lot of smaller cities and towns and rural areas like Butler County, where there was the rally earlier this summer where somebody tried to assassinate him.
sentences.zh: 他正在走访许多较小的城市、城镇和农村地区，比如巴特勒县，今年夏天早些时候就有人在那里集会上试图暗杀他。

sentences.en: He is going all-in on this working-class vote.
sentences.zh: 他正全力争取这部分工薪阶层的选票。

sentences.en: But here's the trick with that.
sentences.zh: 但这里有个问题。

sentences.en: That share of Pennsylvania's population is shrinking.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州这一群体的人口比例正在缩小。

sentences.en: About 20 years ago, that was about 70% of the population.
sentences.zh: 大约20年前，这大概占总人口的70%。

sentences.en: Now, it's just a hair over 50.
sentences.zh: 现在，刚过50%。

sentences.en: The non-college vote.
sentences.zh: 非大学学历的选票。

sentences.en: The white non-college vote.
sentences.zh: 白人非大学学历选票。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, that's a big decline.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的下降。

sentences.en: And why is that share of the electorate shrinking?
sentences.zh: 为什么这部分选民比例在缩小？

sentences.en: What's happening there?
sentences.zh: 那里发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the rural parts of Pennsylvania, the population in those counties tends to be pretty old.
sentences.zh: 嗯，宾夕法尼亚州的农村地区，这些县的人口往往非常老龄化。

sentences.en: And the younger generation just isn't sticking around.
sentences.zh: 而年轻一代根本不愿留下来。

sentences.en: They're not the jobs there.
sentences.zh: 那里没有工作岗位。

sentences.en: The factories have gone.
sentences.zh: 工厂没了。

sentences.en: The mills have gone.
sentences.zh: 钢厂没了。

sentences.en: Farming is just less and less sustainable.
sentences.zh: 农业变得越来越不可持续。

sentences.en: And so, there's this slow exodus of young people to find better opportunities.
sentences.zh: 因此，年轻人正缓缓外流去寻找更好的机会。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the southeastern corner of the state, outside of Philly, including all the way over to Harrisburg, the suburbs are growing.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，该州东南部、费城郊外，一直延伸到哈里斯堡，郊区正在不断发展。

sentences.en: Suburbs produce exurbs.
sentences.zh: 郊区向外延伸出卫星城。

sentences.en: And they're just expanding out into these once quiet rural counties.
sentences.zh: 它们正在向这些曾经安静的农村县份不断扩张。

sentences.en: And a lot of the people moving into these areas are college-educated professionals.
sentences.zh: 搬进这些地区的许多人都是受过大学教育的专业人士。

sentences.en: They're not working on farMs.
sentences.zh: 他们不种地。

sentences.en: They're working in hospitals or universities, which are now some of the biggest employers in the state.
sentences.zh: 他们在医院或大学工作，而这些现在是该州最大的几家雇主。

sentences.en: Okay, so, rural, working-class voters, in other words, voters without a college degree, continue to move toward the Republican Party in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 好的，也就是说，农村的工薪阶层选民，换句话说就是没有大学学历的选民，在宾夕法尼亚州继续向共和党靠拢。

sentences.en: But there are just fewer of those voters in the state.
sentences.zh: 但州内这类选民变少了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, more educated voters are moving into these areas, and they tend to vote Democrat.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，更多受过教育的选民正搬进这些地区，他们往往投票给民主党。

sentences.en: And that is the big math problem for this election, and maybe for election cycles going forward.
sentences.zh: 这就是这次选举的重大数学难题，或许也是未来选举周期的难题。

sentences.en: Because, remember, in 2020, between Joe Biden and Donald Trump, we're 80,000 votes.
sentences.zh: 因为记住，在2020年，乔·拜登和唐纳德·特朗普之间的差距只有8万票。

sentences.en: It's a college stadium.
sentences.zh: 那只够塞满一个大学体育场。

sentences.en: And, you know, we can all see from the polls this year that it is neck and neck.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们从今年的民调中都能看出，双方不相上下。

sentences.en: It's a dead heat.
sentences.zh: 战况极其胶着。

sentences.en: And so, the real question that the election this year might settle to some degree is which of these trends has gone further?
sentences.zh: 因此，今年选举在某种程度上可能解决的真正问题是，哪一种趋势走得更远？

sentences.en: The partisan realignment of non-college-educated voters, these working-class voters,
sentences.zh: 是非大学学历选民、这些工薪阶层选民的党派重组，

sentences.en: that benefit Donald Trump, or the demographic changes, the shrinking of the rural working class, the growth of the suburbs, these changes that benefit the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这有利于唐纳德·特朗普；还是人口结构的变化，农村工薪阶层的萎缩、郊区的增长，这些有利于民主党的改变。

sentences.en: And one of the best places to see these changing demographics and the friction that comes out of that is in Lancaster County in south-central Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 要观察这些人口结构的变化及其所产生的摩擦，最好的地方之一就是宾夕法尼亚州中南部的兰开斯特县。

sentences.en: Now, most of the country knows this as Amish country.
sentences.zh: 现在，全国大多数人都知道这里是阿米什人聚居区。

sentences.en: Amish, Old Order, Mennonites, a lot of these Christian sects there.
sentences.zh: 阿米什人、旧秩序门诺会教徒，那里有许多这样的基督教派别。

sentences.en: Beautiful farmland.
sentences.zh: 美丽的农田。

sentences.en: You have farmer's markets, folks selling jam on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 这里有农夫市场，路边有人卖果酱。

sentences.en: I literally currently have a jar of strawberry jam in my refrigerator right now from Lancaster, Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我现在的冰箱里，字面意义上就放着一罐来自宾夕法尼亚州兰开斯特的草莓果酱。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 你看吧。

sentences.en: That is what most people think of when they think of Lancaster County.
sentences.zh: 这就是大多数人想到兰开斯特县时的第一印象。

sentences.en: But in the middle, there's Lancaster City, which is a pretty hip and multicultural city.
sentences.zh: 但在县城中心，有着兰开斯特市，这是一个相当时髦且多元文化的城市。

sentences.en: It's got two colleges there.
sentences.zh: 那里有两所大学。

sentences.en: You've got a lot of growth in the suburbs of Lancaster City and a lot of young people in these areas.
sentences.zh: 兰开斯特市的郊区正在蓬勃发展，这些地方有很多年轻人。

sentences.en: But in the county beyond the city, it is still very rural with a lot of small conservative towns.
sentences.zh: 但在城市之外的县里，依然非常乡村化，有着许多保守的小镇。

sentences.en: This is a nice little neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的小社区。

sentences.en: A couple of weeks ago, I went to one of these small towns in the countryside with Delhi producer Nina Feldman.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我和《每日新闻》制作人尼娜·费尔德曼一起去了乡间的一个小镇。

sentences.en: A lot of Trump signs.
sentences.zh: 到处都是特朗普的标语。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is pretty solidly Trump country, I think.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得这里基本上可以说是铁杆的特朗普地盘。

sentences.en: And we were looking to talk to lifelong residents to see if they had noticed changes to the county, if they were watching the growth of the city and these suburbs.
sentences.zh: 我们希望采访当地的土著居民，看看他们是否注意到了该县的变化，是否在关注这座城市和这些郊区的发展。

sentences.en: And that's how we met Todd and Deb Adair, who've lived in this area for their whole lives.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们如何遇到了托德和黛布·阿代尔夫妇，他们一生都住在这一地区。

sentences.en: Mr. Adair?
sentences.zh: 阿代尔先生？

sentences.en: Yes, come on in.
sentences.zh: 是的，请进。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: I hope I didn't mess you up with the Phillies game.
sentences.zh: 希望我没有打扰你看费城人队的比赛。

sentences.en: No, I actually have it on now.
sentences.zh: 没有，我其实正开着电视呢。

sentences.en: So tell me about the Adairs.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我们讲讲阿代尔夫妇吧。

sentences.en: So Todd Adair has a long history in the area.
sentences.zh: 托德·阿代尔在这个地区有着长期的家族渊源。

sentences.en: My grandfather was a...
sentences.zh: 我的祖父曾经是……

sentences.en: Worked in a sewing mill, and then my mom's dad was a concreter.
sentences.zh: 在缝纫厂工作过，然后我妈妈的爸爸是个混凝土工。

sentences.en: He comes from a line of tradesmen.
sentences.zh: 他出身于工匠世家。

sentences.en: On our development, we had 20-some kids in our development, so we all played together.
sentences.zh: 在我们那个开发区，当时有二十几个孩子，所以我们都在一块儿玩。

sentences.en: And when he grew up, he remembers just farmland, everywhere you looked.
sentences.zh: 当他长大后，记忆中到处都是农田。

sentences.en: He used to ride his bike around the fields, and you can just go from field to field as far as I could see.
sentences.zh: 他过去常骑着自行车在田野间穿梭，只要放眼望去，田野连着田野，无边无际。

sentences.en: Everybody knew each other.
sentences.zh: 大家都知根知底。

sentences.en: Most of the folks around grew up there, and their parents grew up there.
sentences.zh: 这里的居民大多都在这儿土生土长，他们的父母也一样。

sentences.en: His parents didn't go to college.
sentences.zh: 他的父母没有上过大学。

sentences.en: He didn't either, but he grew up at a time where it was pretty easy to get a good, lifelong job without a college degree.
sentences.zh: 他也没有，但他成长的那个年代，没有大学文凭也很容易找到一份能干一辈子的好工作。

sentences.en: I always had a nudge to be a truck driver for some reason, so turned 21, dating the wife, and just got into trucking, and that was the end of it.
sentences.zh: 我不知怎么的，一直挺想当个卡车司机的，所以到了21岁，跟现在的妻子谈恋爱时，就直接去开了卡车，然后就这么干到现在。

sentences.en: And that's pretty much what I did the last 20-some years.
sentences.zh: 过去二十多年里，我基本上就一直在干这个。

sentences.en: Now he manages a warehouse, and he lives a pretty good life.
sentences.zh: 现在他管理着一个仓库，生活过得相当不错。

sentences.en: Watches baseball, hangs out with his kids and grandkids.
sentences.zh: 看看棒球比赛，陪陪孩子和孙辈。

sentences.en: But he's starting to see a lot of that Lancaster County that he knew change.
sentences.zh: 但他开始发现，他所熟悉的兰开斯特县正在发生很大变化。

sentences.en: Yeah, townhouses, you know, half-and-halves, whatever you want, duplexes, I guess they call them.
sentences.zh: 对，联排别墅，你知道的，半独立式住宅，随你怎么叫，复式公寓吧，他们好像这么叫。

sentences.en: A lot of the fields where he would ride his bike when he was a kid are now housing developments.
sentences.zh: 他小时候骑车兜风的许多田野，现在都成了住宅区。

sentences.en: Big high-dollar homes, $500,000, $600,000, $700,000 homes were popping up, so.
sentences.zh: 大栋的高档住宅如雨后春笋般涌现，50万、60万、70万美元的房子到处都是。

sentences.en: And there are new houses going up almost overnight everywhere you look.
sentences.zh: 而且你放眼望去，几乎一夜之间到处都在建新房。

sentences.en: And how did he feel about that?
sentences.zh: 那他对此有什么感受呢？

sentences.en: I mean, Todd said that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，托德是这么说的。

sentences.en: It's a little strange.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点怪。

sentences.en: You know, you grew up in a place that was so close-knit, where everybody you knew was brought up there and came from families who grew up there.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你在一个关系非常紧密的地方长大，在那里你认识的每个人都是在这儿长大的，他们的家族也世居于此。

sentences.en: And now there are a lot of people moving in from somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 而现在有很多人从外地搬了进来。

sentences.en: Half these people, I don't even know who they are.
sentences.zh: 这些人的半数，我甚至都不认识是谁。

sentences.en: You see license plates from all over the NortheaSt.
sentences.zh: 你到处能看到来自东北部各州的汽车牌照。

sentences.en: It could be people coming in for jobs from the cities.
sentences.zh: 这些人可能是从城市来这里找工作的。

sentences.en: A lot of them were coming out of state to the jobs, since we're right at Allentown, we're at Philly, we're at Harrisburg, easy rides.
sentences.zh: 他们当中很多人都是从外州过来上班的，因为我们离阿伦敦很近，离费城很近，离哈里斯堡也很近，通勤很方便。

sentences.en: But when I pressed Todd about whether all these people coming in were changing the culture of the place.
sentences.zh: 但当我追问托德，所有这些新来的人是否正在改变当地的文化时。

sentences.en: Yeah, you can see the out-of-towners moving in, but I don't see a big change in the lifestyles.
sentences.zh: 对，你能看到外地人搬进来，但我没看到生活方式有什么大变化。

sentences.en: He pushed back pretty hard.
sentences.zh: 他的反驳相当坚决。

sentences.en: I don't think this area would allow it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个地方不会允许这种改变发生。

sentences.en: And he said that he did not see the basic politics of Lancaster County changing.
sentences.zh: 而且他说，他没看出兰开斯特县的基本政治倾向有什么变化。

sentences.en: Just in voting.
sentences.zh: 也就投票时能看出来。

sentences.en: I mean, I just don't think they'll, we don't support certain values.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我只是觉得他们不会……我们不支持某些价值观。

sentences.en: So, it's dominantly Republican here.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里还是以共和党为主。

sentences.en: Got the Amish.
sentences.zh: 还有阿米什人。

sentences.en: They keep the town pretty straight.
sentences.zh: 他们把镇里管得很正派。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I just got faith in our community.
sentences.zh: 我对我们的社区就是有信心。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a good town to grow up in, and a good area to grow up in, and I think it'll be fine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个适合长大的好镇子，一个适合长大的好地方，我觉得一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: So, by this time in the conversation, Todd's wife, Deb, had come home from work.
sentences.zh: 就在聊到这儿的时候，托德的妻子黛比下班回家了。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: And while we were talking in front of the TV with a game, she was fixing supper behind us in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 正当我们开着电视、放着比赛聊天时，她在我们身后的厨房里准备晚饭。

sentences.en: So, Deb, does the growth in all the newcomers around here, does that worry you?
sentences.zh: 那么，黛比，这里涌现这么多新人，这事儿会让你担心吗？

sentences.en: Do you?
sentences.zh: 你会吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 会啊。

sentences.en: I'm a nurse.
sentences.zh: 我是个护士。

sentences.en: Nothing does.
sentences.zh: 没什么好担心的。

sentences.en: Well, maybe worry's the wrong word.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许“担心”这个词用得不太对。

sentences.en: But what do you make of it?
sentences.zh: 但你是怎么看的？

sentences.en: It does kind of worry me.
sentences.zh: 我确实有点担心。

sentences.en: And she said that from her perspective, things were definitely changing around here.
sentences.zh: 她表示，从她的角度来看，这里的事情确实在发生变化。

sentences.en: A growth in different cultures.
sentences.zh: 不同文化的融合在增长。

sentences.en: And the only thing that worries me most about that is, you know, if they're coming in from Philly or the inner cities, and then they're coming out here,
sentences.zh: 对此我最担心的一点是，你知道的，如果他们是从费城或内城搬出来的，然后搬到我们这儿，

sentences.en: what else are they bringing with them?
sentences.zh: 他们还会带来什么别的东西吗？

sentences.en: She sort of talked in broader terms about her concerns about these newcomers.
sentences.zh: 她用更广泛的视角谈了她对这些新来者的担忧。

sentences.en: But as the conversation went on,
sentences.zh: 但随着谈话的继续，

sentences.en: Deb and Todd started to talk about a kind of general culture that they thought really ran counter to the conservative values that were so important to longtime residents of Lancaster County.
sentences.zh: 黛比和托德开始谈论一种普遍的文化，他们认为这种文化与保守价值观背道而驰，而保守价值观对兰开斯特县的长期居民来说至关重要。

sentences.en: They give everything to their kids.
sentences.zh: 他们对孩子百依百顺。

sentences.en: And that's where the downfall is, because as they grow up, they've gotten everything they've asked for.
sentences.zh: 问题就出在这儿，因为在他们长大过程中，他们要什么有什么。

sentences.en: They get a car when they're 16, don't have to have a job, and everything else.
sentences.zh: 16岁就给买车，不用找工作，什么都有。

sentences.en: They go to college, don't need a job.
sentences.zh: 上大学也不用找工作。

sentences.en: It's paid for.
sentences.zh: 学费都给付清了。

sentences.en: Good for them.
sentences.zh: 这倒无可厚非。

sentences.en: But then when they come out of school, they, oh, I got to work.
sentences.zh: 但等他们毕业步入社会时，他们就会说，哦，我得工作了。

sentences.en: They described a way of approaching work, of how to raise a family, that was just not the way they did things around here.
sentences.zh: 他们描述了一种对待工作、养育家庭的方式，这跟他们在这里做事的方式截然不同。

sentences.en: I got out of high school making $7 an hour, you know, worked two jobs.
sentences.zh: 我高中毕业时时薪才7美元，你知道的，打两份工。

sentences.en: She worked, and we barely squigged by, you know, mac and cheese and hot dogs was our main course of meals most of the time.
sentences.zh: 她也工作，我们勉强糊口，你知道的，通心粉拌奶酪和热狗是我们大多数时候的主食。

sentences.en: So, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以嘛，你懂的。

sentences.en: And not always with milk.
sentences.zh: 而且还不一定顿顿有牛奶喝。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And they're worried about this becoming the world that their grandkids are going to grow up in.
sentences.zh: 他们担心这里会变成他们孙辈以后要生活的世界。

sentences.en: Oh, I pity my granddaughter if we don't.
sentences.zh: 哦，如果我们不采取行动，我真替我孙女感到难过。

sentences.en: It's not a cultural change that they welcome.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们所欢迎的文化变革。

sentences.en: And they're seeing little signs that people who they think hold these kinds of values are starting to show up in surprising places, especially in the heat of election season.
sentences.zh: 他们开始注意到一些微小的迹象，表明那些他们认为持有这类价值观的人开始出现在意想不到的地方，尤其是在激烈的选举季里。

sentences.en: It's to the point.
sentences.zh: 甚至到了这种地步。

sentences.en: For example, they told a story about going to the local fair.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们讲了一个去当地集市的故事。

sentences.en: She was walking through the fair with our Trump sign because that's where we get it every year.
sentences.zh: 她拿着我们的特朗普竞选标语牌走在集市里，因为我们每年都是在那儿领的。

sentences.en: In past years, they've gone here to get Trump campaign signs.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几年里，他们都是去那里领取特朗普的竞选标语牌。

sentences.en: And so Deb went to do the same thing this year.
sentences.zh: 所以今年黛比也去拿了标语牌。

sentences.en: She got a Trump campaign sign, and she was walking through the fair.
sentences.zh: 她拿了特朗普的竞选标语牌，正走在集市里。

sentences.en: And a lady made a comment to her about her carrying the sign.
sentences.zh: 有个女人对她拿着标语牌一事评头论足了一番。

sentences.en: And she gave me the, like, but really now?
sentences.zh: 然后她看着我，那表情就像是在说，不会吧？

sentences.en: And I'm like, we all have our own choices.
sentences.zh: 而我的反应是，我们都有自己的选择。

sentences.en: And somebody saw her with a sign and gave her this look, like, really?
sentences.zh: 有人看到她拿着标语牌，就投来那种眼神，仿佛在说：真的假的？

sentences.en: As in, like, you're voting for Trump?
sentences.zh: 那意思就像是：你在给特朗普投票？

sentences.en: Yeah, in this very conservative little town.
sentences.zh: 对，在这个极其保守的小镇里。

sentences.en: And she turned and said, well, we can all make our own decisions.
sentences.zh: 她转过身说，嗯，我们每个人都能做自己的决定。

sentences.en: Did you recognize her?
sentences.zh: 你认识她吗？

sentences.en: No, I've never seen her.
sentences.zh: 不认识，我从没见过她。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不认识。

sentences.en: And you don't think that would have happened two years ago, three years ago?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这种事在两三年前会发生吗？

sentences.en: Nah.
sentences.zh: 才不会呢。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不知道。

sentences.en: It's a little thing.
sentences.zh: 这只是一件小事。

sentences.en: It's subtle.
sentences.zh: 很不显眼。

sentences.en: It was this one encounter.
sentences.zh: 只是这么一次小小的偶遇。

sentences.en: But it did seem to speak to a kind of culture clash that is brought by all these new people moving into Lancaster County.
sentences.zh: 但它确实反映出了一种文化冲突，是由所有这些搬到兰开斯特县的新居民带来的。

sentences.en: And that made us want to go meet some of them.
sentences.zh: 这让我们很想去见见他们中的一些人。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏板块字谜游戏“连接（Connections）”的创作者。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天负责制作“拼字蜜蜂（Spelling Bee）”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色听联觉的病症。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到声音的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: So, Campbell, tell me about these newcomers who've moved into Lancaster County.
sentences.zh: 那么，坎贝尔，跟我讲讲这些搬到兰开斯特县的新居民吧。

sentences.en: So, outside of Lancaster City, when you drive around the farmland, you see a lot of new housing developments popping up.
sentences.zh: 所以，在兰开斯特市外围，当你开车穿过农田时，你会看到许多新建的住宅区拔地而起。

sentences.en: Some are for these, you know, upper-scale working professionals who moved from the city out to the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 有些是为那些从城市搬到郊区的高端工薪专业人士准备的。

sentences.en: But there are a lot of retirement communities.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多是退休社区。

sentences.en: Now, when you think of ex-urban sprawl, you don't necessarily think of retirees, but they're a big part of the shift.
sentences.zh: 说到城郊扩张，你未必会联想到退休人员，但他们却是这种转变的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: And many of the retirees living in these communities are college-educated.
sentences.zh: 而且这些社区里的许多退休人员都受过大学教育。

sentences.en: Like, maybe they grew up there, they're moving back, or maybe they're moving there from New York or New Jersey, Long Island.
sentences.zh: 比如，也许他们原本就在这儿长大，现在又搬了回来，或者他们是从纽约、新泽西或长岛搬过来的。

sentences.en: Pennsylvania has very retirement-friendly tax structure.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州的税收政策对退休人员非常友好。

sentences.en: It's cheaper, it's beautiful, there's good access to health care.
sentences.zh: 这里生活成本更低、风景优美，医疗服务也很便利。

sentences.en: Is this a two-way street?
sentences.zh: 这是一个双向的过程吗？

sentences.en: I hope so.
sentences.zh: 但愿如此。

sentences.en: There was no sign.
sentences.zh: 没有任何标志。

sentences.en: And one of these retirement communities is not too far from where Todd and Deb live, on the edge of a little town called Ephrata.
sentences.zh: 其中一个退休社区离托德和黛比住的地方不远，位于一个叫埃夫拉塔的小镇边缘。

sentences.en: So the development is in what was clearly probably a cornfield 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以这个开发项目所在地，在20年前显然可能还是一片玉米地。

sentences.en: The houses are well-appointed, they're newish, it's about a dozen years old.
sentences.zh: 这里的房子设施齐全、比较新，大约有十二年历史了。

sentences.en: The streets have names like Liberty and Freedom and Tradition.
sentences.zh: 街道的名字都叫“自由”、“独立”和“传统”之类的。

sentences.en: There are well-manicured lawns and front porches with a lot of Halloween decor.
sentences.zh: 这里有修剪整齐的草坪和带有大量万圣节装饰的前廊。

sentences.en: And so we went to talk to a group of women who live in one of these communities.
sentences.zh: 于是我们去采访了一群住在其中一个社区的女性。

sentences.en: And is it farmland past here?
sentences.zh: 这里过去是农田吗？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Beautiful farms, yeah.
sentences.zh: 美丽的农场，是的。

sentences.en: They're all neighbors, ten of them that we met, all in their 60s and 70s.
sentences.zh: 她们都是邻居，我们见到了十个人，年龄都在60岁到70岁之间。

sentences.en: Meals got out of their Kenston paddock.
sentences.zh: 山羊从肯斯顿围场里跑出来了。

sentences.en: They were chewing our neighbor's lawn.
sentences.zh: 它们在啃我们邻居的草坪。

sentences.en: A lot of whom moved into Lancaster County in the last few years.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有很多人是在过去几年里搬到兰开斯特县的。

sentences.en: Every group I belonged to was all Trump supporters.
sentences.zh: 我加入过的每一个群体里所有人都是特朗普的支持者。

sentences.en: We went to chat with them.
sentences.zh: 我们去和她们聊了聊。

sentences.en: They were meeting in what they called their, quote, support group.
sentences.zh: 她们是在她们所谓的“互助小组”里碰面的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: They told us before they found each other, when they first moved here, most of them, they very quickly discovered that they really were political outsiders.
sentences.zh: 她们告诉我们，在刚搬到这里、还没找到彼此之前，她们大多数人很快就发现自己其实是政治上的局外人。

sentences.en: Like, I swim at the rec center.
sentences.zh: 比如，我在休闲中心游泳。

sentences.en: They're all talking about Trump all the time.
sentences.zh: 大家总是在谈论特朗普。

sentences.en: I had a women's group.
sentences.zh: 我参加过一个女性小组。

sentences.en: They all love Trump.
sentences.zh: 她们都喜欢特朗普。

sentences.en: One of them was Sharon Nelson.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是莎伦·纳尔逊。

sentences.en: She lived there the longest, almost 10 years.
sentences.zh: 她在这里住的时间最长，将近10年。

sentences.en: And she said that every group of people she found herself in, they were all talking about how much they loved Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 她说，无论她身处哪个群体，大家都在讨论他们有多么热爱唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And I felt very alone or like an outcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己非常孤独，就像个局外人。

sentences.en: I'm like, why do I not fit in in any of these places?
sentences.zh: 我在想，为什么我在这些地方都格格不入？

sentences.en: And for a while, they thought they were on an island.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，她们觉得自己就像孤岛一样。

sentences.en: They just kept their mouths shut.
sentences.zh: 她们只能三缄其口。

sentences.en: I moved here from Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我是从弗吉尼亚搬来的。

sentences.en: I lived on the northern neck of Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我住在弗吉尼亚北部颈地。

sentences.en: Everyone had a gun.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有枪。

sentences.en: Everyone was for Trump.
sentences.zh: 每个人都支持特朗普。

sentences.en: Another one was Suki Starkey.
sentences.zh: 还有一个人是苏基·斯塔基。

sentences.en: She moved there more recently.
sentences.zh: 她搬到那里的时间比较近。

sentences.en: She wanted to be near her kids.
sentences.zh: 她想离孩子们近一点。

sentences.en: So I thought, yes, I'm going to get out of this hellhole.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，是的，我要离开这个鬼地方。

sentences.en: And she thought, moving from rural Virginia, she would find a different political mix.
sentences.zh: 她以为，从弗吉尼亚州的农村搬过去，会遇到不同的政治组合。

sentences.en: And we moved here.
sentences.zh: 于是我们搬到了这里。

sentences.en: And I thought, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 我心想，天哪。

sentences.en: You know, this is like a repeat of what I had in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这简直就像我在弗吉尼亚经历的重演。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 真的是这样。

sentences.en: But almost everyone around her seemed to be Trump supporters.
sentences.zh: 但她周围几乎所有人似乎都是特朗普的支持者。

sentences.en: I thought, I've got to get out of here.
sentences.zh: 我心想，我得离开这里。

sentences.en: These people are going to, you know, eat me alive.
sentences.zh: 这些人会，你知道的，把我活吞了。

sentences.en: Until I found these nice people.
sentences.zh: 直到我遇到了这些好心人。

sentences.en: So, slowly but surely, in little ways, it's almost like a nod, nod, wink, wink situation.
sentences.zh: 所以，慢慢地、稳妥地，通过一些小细节，这几乎成了一种心照不宣、彼此会意的局面。

sentences.en: They'd find out that there were other Democrats in their community.
sentences.zh: 他们会发现社区里还有其他民主党人。

sentences.en: How would you know?
sentences.zh: 你怎么会知道？

sentences.en: How would it come up?
sentences.zh: 这怎么会聊起来呢？

sentences.en: Just very subtle ways, you know.
sentences.zh: 就是通过非常微妙的方式，你知道的。

sentences.en: It is almost like a vibe.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是一种磁场。

sentences.en: Don't you think?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: It wasn't easy figuring this out.
sentences.zh: 要搞清楚这一点并不容易。

sentences.en: There are no lawn signs in their development because it's against the rules there.
sentences.zh: 他们的住宅区里没有任何草坪标语，因为这里不允许。

sentences.en: So, they had to kind of get a vibe to know who the other Democrats might be.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们必须靠某种直觉来辨别谁可能是其他民主党人。

sentences.en: My husband and I, or either one of us, would have a conversation with somebody else that was like-minded.
sentences.zh: 我和我丈夫，或者我们俩中的某个人，会和另一个志同道合的人聊天。

sentences.en: We'd, like, run home.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就会，比如说，一路小跑回家。

sentences.en: We had a big secret, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们怀揣着一个巨大的秘密。

sentences.en: Hey, guess what?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: I just talked to so-and-so.
sentences.zh: 我刚才跟某某聊过了。

sentences.en: And they hate Trump, too.
sentences.zh: 他们也讨厌特朗普。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They're not a MAGA.
sentences.zh: 他们不是MAGA支持者。

sentences.en: They're not a MAGA.
sentences.zh: 他们才不是MAGA。

sentences.en: They'd be going out to get the mail or seeing somebody doing the lawn, and they'd have a quick conversation.
sentences.zh: 他们会在出门取信或者看到有人在修剪草坪时，简单聊上几句。

sentences.en: And somebody had said something that would give them the vibe like, oh, this might be another Democrat.
sentences.zh: 然后有人会说一些话，透出那种气息，哦，这可能又是个民主党人。

sentences.en: And then in June...
sentences.zh: 然后在六月……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: We started getting together because...
sentences.zh: 我们开始聚在一起，因为……

sentences.en: Mental health.
sentences.zh: 心理健康。

sentences.en: And mental health.
sentences.zh: 为了心理健康。

sentences.en: When, after the...
sentences.zh: 当在经历了……

sentences.en: After that Biden debate, when Democrats all over the country were really at a low point, one of them reached out and said,
sentences.zh: 在拜登那场辩论之后，当全国各地的民主党人真的处于低谷时，其中一人联系了大家并说道：

sentences.en: do y'all want to get together for a support group to talk about this?
sentences.zh: 你们大家想不想聚在一起搞个互助小组来聊聊这事？

sentences.en: And so they did.
sentences.zh: 于是他们真的这么做了。

sentences.en: Our very first meeting was when Biden announced that he was dropping out.
sentences.zh: 我们的第一次聚会正好赶上拜登宣布退选。

sentences.en: So we kind of...
sentences.zh: 所以我们有点……

sentences.en: So they started getting together, and little by little, others would find out about the group,
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始聚会，渐渐地，其他人也知道了这个小组的存在，

sentences.en: and the group was getting bigger and bigger, especially in a place that they had previously thought was just all Trump supporters.
sentences.zh: 而且这个组织越来越大，尤其是在一个他们以前认为全都是特朗普支持者的地方。

sentences.en: I kept my mouth shut for, like, 10 years or however long it's been, and finally I'm like, you know what?
sentences.zh: 我闭口不言了大概有10年，或者不管过去多久，最后我心想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I'm not hiding anymore.
sentences.zh: 我再也不躲藏了。

sentences.en: So what started as a support group, eventually as it got bigger, became a group where they would organize things.
sentences.zh: 所以，最初作为一个互助小组，随着规模越来越大，它最终变成了一个他们用来组织活动的团体。

sentences.en: We were even talking about doing post-it notes and putting them in the ladies' restroom.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至讨论过做一些便利贴，贴在女士洗手间里。

sentences.en: And you close...
sentences.zh: 当你关上……

sentences.en: You close the stall and there's a note saying...
sentences.zh: 当你关上隔间门，上面会有一张纸条写着……

sentences.en: Your vote is private.
sentences.zh: 你的投票是私密的。

sentences.en: And they start volunteering for the Harris campaign.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始为哈里斯的竞选团队当志愿者。

sentences.en: So the Harris campaign is there in that area?
sentences.zh: 所以哈里斯的竞选团队就在那个地区吗？

sentences.en: For the first time, actually, in a Democratic presidential campaign, the Harris campaign has a full-time staffed office in this part of Lancaster County.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在民主党总统竞选历史上，哈里斯的竞选团队首次在兰开斯特县的这一地区设立了全职员工办公室。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 真有意思。

sentences.en: So they are also noting this demographic change, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 看来他们也注意到了这种人口结构的变化。

sentences.en: Yeah, and while they probably don't think they can win this county this year, Trump won it by 16 points in 2020.
sentences.zh: 是的，虽然他们可能觉得今年赢不了这个县——特朗普在2020年以16个百分点的优势赢了这里——

sentences.en: They see where this trend is going, and they're sending out huge teams of door knockers in even this part of the county and doing a lot of get out the vote.
sentences.zh: 但他们看到了这种趋势的发展方向，他们甚至在这个县的这一地区派出了庞大的拉票团队，做了大量动员投票的工作。

sentences.en: So the women in this support group had been volunteering and door knocking and doing all the campaign stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以这个互助小组里的女性一直在做志愿者、挨家挨户敲门拉票，做所有竞选相关的事情。

sentences.en: But on the night that we met them...
sentences.zh: 但就在我们见到他们的那天晚上……

sentences.en: It's misting out of here.
sentences.zh: 外面在下毛毛雨。

sentences.en: I didn't bring an umbral.
sentences.zh: 我没带伞。

sentences.en: Maybe I should.
sentences.zh: 也许我该带一把。

sentences.en: They were also preparing to walk alongside the Democratic Party float in the big annual parade in downtown Ephrata.
sentences.zh: 他们还准备在伊夫拉塔市中心一年一度的大游行中，伴随民主党的花车一起游行。

sentences.en: We're getting wet for Kamala.
sentences.zh: 我们为了卡玛拉淋湿也在所不惜。

sentences.en: I'm going to get my hat.
sentences.zh: 我要去拿我的帽子。

sentences.en: Now, this was a big step.
sentences.zh: 这可是一大步。

sentences.en: I mean, it's one thing to go knock on the doors of people you know are registered Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，去敲那些你知道已经登记为民主党人的门是一回事。

sentences.en: You're working off your liSt.
sentences.zh: 你是按着名单在工作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's another thing to walk right through downtown with a Harris-Waltz shirt on.
sentences.zh: 但穿着印有“哈里斯-沃尔兹”的衬衫直接穿过市中心又是另一回事了。

sentences.en: They, like, came fully out of the closet.
sentences.zh: 他们简直是彻底公开了。

sentences.en: This was the big coming-out moment.
sentences.zh: 这是他们盛大的出柜时刻。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I hope they don't yell things.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们不要大喊大叫。

sentences.en: Because I'm very sensitive.
sentences.zh: 因为我很敏感。

sentences.en: And they were a little nervous.
sentences.zh: 他们当时有点紧张。

sentences.en: I feel like there's going to be people out there going to be yelling at us.
sentences.zh: 我觉得外面会有人对我们大喊大叫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And maybe even somebody will throw something at us.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能有人会向我们扔东西。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Jeez, Marilyn.
sentences.zh: 天哪，玛丽莲。

sentences.en: And there were some worries about getting booed and heckled during the parade.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至担心在游行期间会被嘘、会被起哄。

sentences.en: And some even thought that these kids who have hands full of Tootsie Rolls that were thrown out before they passed by would throw them at them as they walked by.
sentences.zh: 还有人甚至认为，那些手里拿着在游行队伍经过前分发的图茨罗尔糖果的孩子们，会在他们走过时把糖砸向他们。

sentences.en: Ow.
sentences.zh: 哎哟。

sentences.en: Tootsie Roll could hurt.
sentences.zh: 图茨罗尔糖砸下来也是会疼的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Okay, we're organizing.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们在组织队伍了。

sentences.en: So they were concerned about what their reception would be at the parade.
sentences.zh: 所以他们很关心自己在游行中会受到什么样的接待。

sentences.en: All right, I'll see you there.
sentences.zh: 好的，一会儿见。

sentences.en: We're going on a main street through town.
sentences.zh: 我们要穿过镇上的主街。

sentences.en: And people are lying on both sides, sitting in camp chairs.
sentences.zh: 两边都站满了人，还有人坐在露营椅上。

sentences.en: So we went out with them that night and walked alongside the Democratic Party float to see how they would be received.
sentences.zh: 于是那天晚上我们和他们一起出发，陪着民主党的花车同行，看看他们会受到怎样的接待。

sentences.en: And as soon as it started, the float did get booed.
sentences.zh: 刚一出发，花车确实遭到了嘘声。

sentences.en: That was not a surprise.
sentences.zh: 这并不意外。

sentences.en: But as we went on, there were a surprising number of cheers, too.
sentences.zh: 但随着游行继续，也有数量惊人的欢呼声。

sentences.en: So really, these longtime residents coming up against newcomers, this culture clash, that was really on display at the parade.
sentences.zh: 所以真的，这些老居民与新来者的碰撞，这种文化冲突，在游行中真切地展现出来了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and you could see it, like, physically manifest along the route of the parade.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以看到它沿着游行路线具象化地表现出来。

sentences.en: So we just walked by a duplex.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚走过一栋复式住宅。

sentences.en: And what first drew my eye was a bunch of Trump flags, a big sign that said Trump was right.
sentences.zh: 最先吸引我眼球的是一堆特朗普的旗子，还有一个写着“特朗普是对的”的大标语。

sentences.en: The usual patriotic Trump signs.
sentences.zh: 那些常见的爱国风特朗普标语。

sentences.en: And in the other half of the duplex was a giant rainbow flag.
sentences.zh: 而在复式住宅的另一半，则挂着一面巨大的彩虹旗。

sentences.en: I stopped by to the man sitting in front of the rainbow flag house.
sentences.zh: 我走到坐在彩虹旗房子门前的那位男士旁边。

sentences.en: And I said, how's this work out?
sentences.zh: 我问他，这怎么调和得好？

sentences.en: He said, a lot of friction.
sentences.zh: 他说，有相当多的摩擦。

sentences.en: So as the night went along, the women in the support group, who were marching alongside the float, were feeling pretty good about things.
sentences.zh: 随着夜幕降临，伴随花车游行的互助小组成员们对情况感到相当不错。

sentences.en: What's your sense of the crowd response been?
sentences.zh: 你觉得人群的反应怎么样？

sentences.en: Well, I was surprised how positive it was.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我挺意外反应会这么积极。

sentences.en: I mean, there was a negative, but a lot of people gave us, you know, the big waves and high fives and everything.
sentences.zh: 我是说，虽然有负面的声音，但很多人都向我们，你知道的，大力挥手、击掌什么的。

sentences.en: So did you get anything thrown at you?
sentences.zh: 那你们有没有被扔什么东西？

sentences.en: Pardon?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Did you get, no?
sentences.zh: 你们有没有被，没有吗？

sentences.en: I don't think many people threw Tootsie Rolls, and they felt like the night really was a success.
sentences.zh: 我觉得没多少人扔图茨罗尔糖，他们觉得今晚真的挺成功的。

sentences.en: And then we were coming right down Main Street into the heart of town, and we were passing by a big,
sentences.zh: 然后我们径直沿着主街来到镇中心，路过了一栋宏伟、

sentences.en: beautiful old house with a wraparound porch strung up with garden lights and a packed front yard, big kind of a tailgate.
sentences.zh: 漂亮的旧房子，它有着环绕式的门廊，上面挂着花园串灯，前院挤满了人，搞得像个大型赛前尾门派对。

sentences.en: And they began shouting at the Democratic float.
sentences.zh: 他们开始向民主党花车大喊大叫。

sentences.en: So we stopped by to talk to the guy who was sort of leading the chance, a guy named Brian Keith.
sentences.zh: 于是我们停下来和那个带头喊口号的人聊了聊，他叫布赖恩·基斯。

sentences.en: He was hosting this huge party.
sentences.zh: 他在主办这个盛大的派对。

sentences.en: This is the place they hate to come by, yes.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们讨厌经过的地方，是的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, we're not, yeah, it's pretty obvious who we support.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们不是，嗯，我们支持谁其实挺明显的。

sentences.en: So Brian is a Republican who's voted for Trump.
sentences.zh: 布赖恩是一位投过特朗普票的共和党人。

sentences.en: He doesn't love the guy, but he is a conservative libertarian, as he calls himself.
sentences.zh: 他并不是多喜欢这个人，但他用他自己的话说，是一个保守派自由意志主义者。

sentences.en: So, Ephrata fit me, I'm a hunter, I'm a fisherman, you know, the whole motorcycles, 4x4s, that whole thing, and this, this one.
sentences.zh: 所以，伊夫拉塔很适合我，我是个猎人，我是个渔夫，你知道的，各种摩托车、四轮驱动车，就是那一套，还有这个，这个地方。

sentences.en: He didn't grow up in Lancaster County.
sentences.zh: 他不是在兰开斯特县长大的。

sentences.en: And I'm like, I'm more of the redneck-y guy that Ephrata made more sense.
sentences.zh: 我更像是个乡巴佬类型的人，伊夫拉塔对我来说更有意义。

sentences.en: But he loves this part of the county because of what he sees as its values.
sentences.zh: 但他很喜欢这个县的这一部分，因为他看到了这里所珍视的价值观。

sentences.en: It's a different city than it was 15 years ago, which isn't actually a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 这里的城市已经和15年前不同了，这其实并不是一件坏事。

sentences.en: It's just demographically, it's different than it was.
sentences.zh: 只是在人口结构上，它跟过去不一样了。

sentences.en: And so we wanted to know what he makes of these newcomers moving in.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想知道他是怎么看待这些搬进来的新来者的。

sentences.en: It's Ephrata, Pennsylvania, which was a Mennonite, white-bred community type of thing, right?
sentences.zh: 这里是宾夕法尼亚州的伊夫拉塔，曾经是一个门诺派的、全白人的纯粹社区，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now it's very much a diverse community.
sentences.zh: 现在它在很大程度上是一个多元化的社区。

sentences.en: Not that that's a bad thing, but it's changed with the cost of living.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说这是件坏事，但它随着生活成本发生了变化。

sentences.en: Everything else that's happened here, it's kind of gone hand in hand.
sentences.zh: 这里发生的一切，其实都是息息相关的。

sentences.en: He told us, unlike Todd Adair, that all these little changes, the new people moving in, the prices going up, the different cultural views, that they really are adding up for him.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我们，跟托德·阿代尔不同，所有这些细微的变化、新人的搬入、物价的上涨、不同的文化观点，对他来说真的积少成多，让他吃不消了。

sentences.en: Do you think that the Democrats didn't have a chance this time in Lancaster County?
sentences.zh: 你觉得民主党这次在兰开斯特县没有机会吗？

sentences.en: Is it like a change this time around?
sentences.zh: 这次情况会有所改变吗？

sentences.en: So the demographics change enough that people are moving out of the cities, that type of thing, where this county eventually will be a blue, will be a blue linen county.
sentences.zh: 所以人口结构的变化足够大，人们搬出了城市，诸如此类，以至于这个县最终会变成一个蓝色，变成一个民主党倾向的县。

sentences.en: So much that he told us that he's starting to see the writing on the wall.
sentences.zh: 以至于他告诉我们，他开始看到大势已去了。

sentences.en: We're my wife's real estate agent.
sentences.zh: 我们是我妻子的房产经纪人。

sentences.en: We've lived here 17 years.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里住了17年。

sentences.en: We're looking at getting the heck out of town.
sentences.zh: 我们正考虑赶快离开这个镇。

sentences.en: Are y'all thinking about moving out because y'all don't like the changes in Ephrata?
sentences.zh: 你们在考虑搬走是因为你们不喜欢伊夫拉塔的变化吗？

sentences.en: And that he's already thinking of moving farther out into the country.
sentences.zh: 而且他已经在考虑搬到更远的乡村去了。

sentences.en: Give it another 10 years and it's going to be, we're going to be out in Alberta.
sentences.zh: 再过10年，就会变成，我们要搬到阿尔伯塔去了。

sentences.en: So he is very different than Todd then.
sentences.zh: 所以他跟托德很不一样呢。

sentences.en: Todd saw changes and felt like they didn't really amount to much.
sentences.zh: 托德看到了变化，但觉得这些变化其实没多大影响。

sentences.en: And Brian's saying, this is fundamentally changing my town.
sentences.zh: 而布赖恩则说，这正在从根本上改变我的小镇。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So which of them is right, Todd or Brian?
sentences.zh: 那么他们两个谁是对的，托德还是布赖恩？

sentences.en: I mean, how much do these shifts actually matter?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些转变到底有多大关系？

sentences.en: Well, Todd is right in the sense that the white working class is still the majority in Lancaster County and actually in the state of Pennsylvania as a whole.
sentences.zh: 嗯，托德说得对，因为白人工人阶级在兰开斯特县以及整个宾夕法尼亚州仍然占多数。

sentences.en: But Brian is right in the sense that this is moving in one direction.
sentences.zh: 但布赖恩说得对，因为这种变化正朝着一个方向发展。

sentences.en: The working class population is shrinking year by year.
sentences.zh: 工人阶级人口逐年萎缩。

sentences.en: And this population of college-educated professionals tend to be more democratic is growing.
sentences.zh: 而受过大学教育的专业人士群体——他们往往更倾向于民主党——正在不断壮大。

sentences.en: And that math is not on the side of the Trump coalition.
sentences.zh: 这种人口结构对特朗普阵营并不有利。

sentences.en: So this trend is moving in the wrong direction for Trump.
sentences.zh: 所以对特朗普来说，这个趋势正朝着错误的方向发展。

sentences.en: What's he going to do about it?
sentences.zh: 他打算怎么应对？

sentences.en: Well, Trump knows that if he wants to keep Pennsylvania in play for the Republicans, he needs to expand his base.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特朗普知道，如果他想让宾夕法尼亚州继续成为共和党争夺的目标，他就必须扩大其支持基础。

sentences.en: It would still be a working class base, mainly of folks who don't have college degrees.
sentences.zh: 这仍然会是一个工人阶级的基础，主要由没有大学学历的人组成。

sentences.en: But you can see the campaign already making inroads or trying to make inroads with other groups,
sentences.zh: 但你可以看到，竞选团队已经在努力打入或尝试打入其他群体，

sentences.en: Latinos in the small cities in eastern Pennsylvania or a young black man in cities like Philadelphia,
sentences.zh: 比如宾夕法尼亚州东部小城市的拉丁裔，或是费城等城市的年轻黑人男性，

sentences.en: because he and his campaign realized that the working class white base is shrinking.
sentences.zh: 因为他和他的竞选团队意识到，白人工人阶级的基本盘正在缩小。

sentences.en: And so they're going to have to pick up votes from somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们必须从其他地方争取选票。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's looking for these working class people in other demographic groups.
sentences.zh: 他正在其他人口群体中寻找这些工人阶级的人。

sentences.en: And as we know, he's having some success in that department with black men, with Hispanic men, particularly non-college people.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，他在争取黑人男性、尤其是西班牙裔男性的非大学学历人群方面，已经取得了一些成功。

sentences.en: And if he pulls it off, that could be just as dangerous a trend for Democrats in the long run.
sentences.zh: 如果他成功了，从长远来看，这对民主党人来说可能是一个同样危险的趋势。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he has to do this because it's not just in Pennsylvania where these shifts are happening.
sentences.zh: 而且他必须这么做，因为发生这种转变的不仅仅是宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: It's happening at different speeds, in different places, but it's happening everywhere.
sentences.zh: 不同地方的发展速度不同，但这种现象无处不在。

sentences.en: I mean, you see it in Michigan, Arizona, Georgia, Wisconsin, all these other swing states.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在密歇根、亚利桑那、佐治亚、威斯康星以及所有这些摇摆州都能看到这一点。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Like Virginia went blue in 2019, and that was very much the same dynamic.
sentences.zh: 就像弗吉尼亚州在2019年变成蓝色一样，当时的情况非常相似。

sentences.en: Non-college voters in the rural parts of the state, which is territorially most of the state,
sentences.zh: 该州农村地区的非大学选民——从地域上看占了该州的大部分——

sentences.en: were just outweighed at a certain point by the college grads moving to those thickly settled areas in northern Virginia.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，人数被搬到弗吉尼亚州北部稠密地区的大学毕业生盖过了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So in some ways, Lancaster County is just a few election cycles behind where Virginia was, where the base is gradually being overtaken by these new, different voters.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，兰开斯特县只是比当年的弗吉尼亚州落后了几场选举，那里的基本盘正逐渐被这些新的、不同的选民所取代。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So if Virginia is like a postcard from the future for Lancaster County, and that postcard would be positive for Democrats,
sentences.zh: 那么，如果说弗吉尼亚州就像是写给兰开斯特县的未来明信片，而这张明信片对民主党来说是积极的，

sentences.en: what could the Democrats do to turn Pennsylvania into Virginia?
sentences.zh: 民主党人可以做些什么来把宾夕法尼亚州变成弗吉尼亚州？

sentences.en: Well, now look, for this election, you know, they're door-knocking and writing postcards
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，对于这次选举，你知道的，他们在敲门、写明信片，

sentences.en: and doing all those things to sort of get those margins a few notches up where they need them.
sentences.zh: 做所有这些事情，好把那些得票差距拉高到他们需要的水平。

sentences.en: But really, in the medium and long term,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，从中长期来看，

sentences.en: Democrats just have to hope that more people, like the women in this support group, you know, college-educated professionals who tend to vote Democrat,
sentences.zh: 民主党人只能寄希望于更多人——比如这个互助小组里的女性，你知道的，那些倾向于投票给民主党的受过大学教育的专业人士——

sentences.en: move into places like Lancaster County and change the politics.
sentences.zh: 搬到兰开斯特县这样地方来，改变那里的政治格局。

sentences.en: On Thursday, former President Donald Trump said that if he was elected president again, he would immediately fire special counsel Jack Smith,
sentences.zh: 周四，前总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，如果他再次当选总统，他将立即解雇特别检察官杰克·史密斯，

sentences.en: who has brought two federal indictments against him.
sentences.zh: 后者对他提起了两项联邦起诉。

sentences.en: Smith has charged Trump with plotting to overturn his 2020 election laws and with illegally holding on to classified material after leaving office.
sentences.zh: 史密斯指控特朗普密谋推翻2020年大选结果，并在卸任后非法保留机密文件。

sentences.zh: 前提是他能再次赢得总统任期。

sentences.en: And the Los Angeles County chief prosecutor requested the resentencing of Lyle and Eric Menendez,

sentences.en: who killed their parents in 1989 after what they said was sexual molestation of them by their father.
sentences.zh: 两人于1989年杀害了他们的父母，此前他们声称曾遭到父亲的性虐待。

sentences.en: Their claims were met with widespread skepticism during their trial.
sentences.zh: 在他们的审判期间，这些说法遭到了广泛的怀疑。

sentences.en: But the case drew renewed attention this year after Netflix released a docudrama about it
sentences.zh: 但在今年Netflix发布了一部关于此案的虚构纪录片之后，该案重新受到了关注，

sentences.en: and later a documentary in which the brothers discuss the case at length in prison interviews.
sentences.zh: 随后又推出了一部纪录片，兄弟俩在狱中采访中详细讨论了此案。

sentences.en: The move, by district attorney George Gascon, could pave the way for the brothers to walk free.
sentences.zh: 地区检察官乔治·加斯科这一举动，可能会为兄弟俩重获自由铺平道路。
